title: Clearing the Snowdrifts
story:
Ingrid's pre-winter checklist, last page:

`[ ] free disk space: the engine is at 94%`
`[ ] keep everything labelled keep=true (Tomasz's cores)`
`[ ] keep whatever is running or in use`

Tomasz has labelled the three things he cannot lose: a stopped container, a volume and an image, all `keep=true`. Everything else that nobody is using must go: stopped containers, unused volumes and dangling images. A bare `prune` would take his data with it, so use label filters.
objectives: Remove every unused volume except `ledger-vol` (label `keep=true`); `gauge-data` is in use and must stay
Remove every dangling image except the one labelled `keep=true`
Leave the running container `snow-gauge` and the tagged images `kestrel/drift:latest` and `kestrel/ledger-snap:latest` untouched
startingState: Three throwaway stopped containers, two unused volumes and a few dangling images are mixed in with the things that must survive. A container `snow-gauge` is running and uses the volume `gauge-data`.
hints: Docker has a `prune` command for each kind of object. Pruning removes only what is unused, and most prune commands accept filters, so you can exclude anything carrying a particular label.

Try `docker container prune`, `docker volume prune` and `docker image prune`, each with `-f` and `--filter "label!=keep=true"`. Since Docker 23, `volume prune` skips named volumes unless you add `--all` (`-a`). Check with `docker ps -a`, `docker volume ls` and `docker images -f dangling=true`.

```bash
docker container prune -f --filter "label!=keep=true"
docker volume prune -af --filter "label!=keep=true"
docker image prune -f --filter "label!=keep=true"

docker ps -a
docker volume ls
docker images -f dangling=true
```

commands: docker run -d --name snow-gauge -v gauge-data:/data alpine:3.20 sleep infinity
for i in 1 2 3; do docker run --name drift-$i alpine:3.20 true; done
docker run --name keeper-log --label keep=true alpine:3.20 true
for v in 1 2; do printf "FROM alpine:3.20\nRUN echo snow-$v > /marker\n" | docker build -q -f - . ; done
printf 'FROM alpine:3.20\nRUN echo drift-tag > /marker\n' | docker build -q -t kestrel/drift:latest -f - .

printf 'FROM alpine:3.20
LABEL keep=true
RUN echo ledger-old > /marker
' | docker build -q -f - .

printf 'FROM alpine:3.20
LABEL keep=true
RUN echo ledger-tag > /marker
' | docker build -q -t kestrel/ledger-snap:latest -f - .

validation.description: Only `keeper-log` remains among the stopped containers

params.command: echo "$(docker images -f dangling=true -q | wc -l | tr -d ' ')/$(docker images -f dangling=true -f label=keep=true -q | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"

validation.description: Exactly one dangling image remains, and it is the one labelled `keep=true`

debrief: Each `prune` removes only what is unused, and `--filter label!=...` lets you fence off whatever you labelled to protect. Pro tip: `--filter until=720h` limits a prune to objects older than 30 days, which makes a safe scheduled job.
